title: Shift the labour market

predict.q: Home deliveries boom, so warehouses want more workers at every wage. What happens?

options.s: The wage rises and employment rises
options.fb: Demand for labour shifts right: at the old wage there is a shortage of workers, so the wage rises (£12 → £14) and more people work (520 → 640).

options.s: The wage rises and employment falls
options.fb: A rise in demand means firms want more workers, so employment rises too.

options.s: The wage falls and employment rises
options.fb: The wage falls when supply rises. Here demand rose, so the wage is pushed up.

options.s: The wage stays the same and employment rises
options.fb: At the old wage there is now a shortage of workers, so the wage rises.

task: Move the "demand for labour" slider right and watch We and Le. Then reset, and move the "supply of labour" slider right and left.

target.do: Move the demand for labour slider to +200, then press Check.

takeaway: A demand shift moves the wage and employment the same way; a supply shift moves them opposite ways.
